channel.title: World
channel.description: The Washington Post World section provides information and analysis of breaking world news stories. In addition to our world news and video, Post World News offers discussions and blogs on major international news and economic issues.

item.title: At least 540 killed in floods; search on for hundreds missing at Nepal-China border
item.dc:creator: Aoife Walsh, Joshua Yang, N. Kirkpatrick
item.description: At least 540 people have been killed and more than 1,500 are reported missing in the Himalayan region as authorities race to find survivors after devastating flash floods.

item.title: Trump’s grab for Greenland rattles Iceland, which considers joining E.U.
item.dc:creator: Ellen Francis, Beatriz Ríos
item.description: Iceland will decide whether to restart talks on joining the European Union in a referendum on Saturday, with President Donald Trump's threat to annex Greenland a motivating factor.

item.title: Volkswagen CEO warns German workers of sweeping layoffs to come
item.dc:creator: Maegan Vazquez
item.description: The automaker, one of the nation’s biggest employers, could shed tens of thousands of jobs amid global market shifts driven by electrification, AI and autonomous driving.

item.title: Uganda declared Ebola-free even as Congo faces deadly, fast-growing epidemic
item.dc:creator: Rael Ombuor
item.description: Uganda's final Ebola patient was discharged from hospital care on July 16.

item.title: Rescuers race to find survivors after Himalayan floods kill more than 350
item.dc:creator: Aoife Walsh, Joshua Yang
item.description: Hundreds of people, including more than 600 tourists, remain missing after the floods hit the Nepal-China border.

item.title: Canada, pressured by Trump, wants new trade partners. Here’s why it’s hard.
item.dc:creator: Sammy Westfall
item.description: The country needs infrastructure and deals to expand exports beyond the United States.

item.title: Why Zelensky is cuddling a very good girl named Freya
item.dc:creator: Victoria Craw
item.description: Pictures of the Ukrainian leader holding the baby pit bull with a symbolic name have proved a truth universally known in politics: If you want to get noticed, get a puppy.

item.title: Ratko Mladic, Bosnian Serb commander found guilty of genocide, dies in prison
item.dc:creator: Roy Gutman
item.description: He was serving a life sentence for his role in the Bosnian War, when he led forces that pounded Sarajevo and carried out the Srebrenica massacre.

item.title: A Venezuelan oilman faced a Swiss arrest warrant. The U.S. had other plans for him.
item.dc:creator: Samuel Oakford, Samantha Schmidt, Anthony Faiola, Karen DeYoung
item.description: The Trump administration intervened in a Swiss criminal investigation of Alejandro Betancourt, who has been helping Washington as an intermediary in Caracas.

item.title: She made history as a trans Indigenous chief. Then addiction cost her the job.
item.dc:creator: Marina Dias, Dan Agostini
item.description: Majur Traytowu is struggling to hold on to influence and authority amid a devastating alcohol epidemic ravaging her territory — and her own life.

item.title: Iran weighs harsh penalties for contact with outside media in ‘foreign influence’ bill
item.dc:creator: Sammy Westfall
item.description: The push comes nearly six months after the U.S. and Israel launched the war, with no immediate diplomatic breakthrough in sight.

item.title: Yayoi Kusama, whose art evoked hallucinatory wonder, dies at 97
item.dc:creator: Juno Carmel
item.description: Her hypnotic, unconventional works propelled her from near-obscurity to a place in the world’s most prominent museums.

item.title: Scores dead, hundreds missing in flash floods on Nepal-China border
item.dc:creator: Joshua Yang
item.description: An avalanche caused the Bhotekoshi River to overflow, sending waves of water and mud that swept buildings and people away.
